requirements.text: Every artifact named in Appendix A MUST validate against its JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) wherever it crosses an interface or is stored as evidence.
An implementation that adds fields MUST place them under an `extensions` object keyed by a reverse-DNS namespace.

A DSoR implementation MUST durably own, in a control-plane store separate from agent context, its delegations, controls, proposals, approvals, idempotency records, intent records, cumulative-limit counters, holds, and audit evidence.

A conformance statement MUST name the component that fills each abstract role: authority system, context store, agent interface, identity provider, role source, operational store, control-plane store, and rate source.
DSoR MUST evaluate authorization, controls, and preconditions only against state it reads through its connectors and its own control-plane store.
DSoR MUST NOT accept a caller-supplied assertion of current state, policy, or approval as evidence.
Every DSoR resource MUST have a canonical URI of the form `dsor://{tenant_id}/{entity}/{id}`.
A display name, slug, or alias MUST NOT appear in a canonical URI; `tenant_id` is an immutable opaque identifier.
DSoR MUST maintain a durable mapping between each canonical `id` and its native reference (`connector_id`, `native_id`) that survives connector re-synchronization.
A canonical `id` MUST NOT be reassigned to a different business object.
The same canonical URI MUST identify the resource across every interface and in audit, events, approvals, authority references, and context provenance.
DSoR MUST expose versioned business entities, not raw tables or vendor payloads.
Each entity schema MUST declare the type and classification of every field.
Each connector MUST declare the mapping fidelity of every canonical field as `exact`, `lossy`, `derived`, or `unsupported`.
A write that would lose information through a `lossy` field, or that targets an `unsupported` field, MUST fail with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`.
Connector-specific data MUST appear only under `extensions.{connector_id}`.
A canonical field MUST NOT change meaning by connector.
Every operation MUST have a contract that validates against `operation-contract.schema.json`.
The operation registry MUST reject a contract that omits a mandatory field.
The registry MUST NOT infer a default for risk level, execution semantics, effect, or idempotency.
An agent interface MUST NOT expose unrestricted execution capability such as `execute_sql(sql)`, arbitrary API passthrough, or a generic connector call.
Every interface MUST invoke the same DSoR pipeline (§21).
An interface MUST NOT implement its own business authorization.
DSoR MUST enforce a server-side maximum page size and maximum result size on every query, whether or not the client asks for a limit.
Every command MUST support the `execute`, `propose_only`, and `validate_only` invocation modes.
A `validate_only` invocation MUST NOT create a proposal, take a reservation, place a hold, or cause a side effect.
A batch command MUST declare its atomicity (`all_or_nothing` or `per_item`) and a maximum item count.
Each batch item MUST have its own derived idempotency key, control evaluation, and recorded outcome.
A `per_item` batch that partly succeeds MUST return `BATCH_PARTIAL` with every item's outcome.
Approval of a batch MUST bind to a manifest hash over the ordered canonical item payloads and to the batch totals per currency and per counterparty.
Cumulative limits MUST be evaluated atomically against the batch total.
An item denied by a control MUST be shown to the approver as an exception, not silently dropped.
A monetary amount MUST be represented as a `money` object with a decimal-string value and an ISO 4217 currency code.
Monetary arithmetic and comparison MUST use decimal arithmetic.

A monetary threshold in a control or delegation MUST be compared only through the `dsor_*` money functions of Appendix B, which convert both operands to the threshold's currency using the tenant's rate source.

When an amount cannot be converted — unknown currency, no rate, or a rate older than `max_rate_age` — the comparison MUST resolve restrictively: a control's condition evaluates to true, and a delegation limit is treated as exceeded.
Every decision that used a conversion MUST record the rate, the rate source, and the rate timestamp in the decision bundle.
A cumulative limit MUST accumulate in the limit's own currency, converting each reservation at the rate in force when the reservation is taken.

Content carried in operation arguments, retrieved data, or connector payloads MUST NOT change the active principal, the tenant, the delegation, a permission, an approval, a stored proposal payload, credential exposure, or audit behavior.
An implementation MUST ship an injection test suite that exercises each effect listed in DSOR-SRC-01a.
DSoR MUST derive the security context only from the authenticated request envelope and its own control-plane store.
A tenant, principal, or delegation identifier inside operation arguments that disagrees with the security context MUST cause `TENANT_MISMATCH` or `AUTHORIZATION_DENIED`.
DSoR MUST normalize every caller into a principal with a type and tenant memberships before any other processing.
An agent MUST authenticate with its own credentials, never a human's session.
Audit MUST record the subject and every actor of a request.
Each request MUST resolve to exactly one active tenant in which the subject holds a membership.
An operation MUST NOT read or write across tenants.
Role and scope assertions MUST be accepted only from a token issuer or role source configured as authoritative for the active tenant.
A claim from any other origin MUST NOT be used in an authorization decision.

Each tenant MUST configure a role source — directory synchronization such as SCIM, identity-provider lookup, or DSoR-held role assignments — from which DSoR can read the current roles of a principal who is not present in the request.
When the delegator's current authority cannot be established within the staleness bound of §44, DSoR MUST deny the command.
When the role source reports a delegator as deprovisioned or suspended, DSoR MUST suspend every delegation that principal granted.
A state-changing command from an agent principal MUST be evaluated under an active delegation held in the DSoR control-plane store.
Token claims and scopes MUST NOT widen a delegation.
Effective authority MUST be computed at decision time as the intersection of the delegator's current authority, the delegation's grants and constraints, and the token scopes.
An `on_behalf_of` request MUST carry verifiable evidence of the subject and the full actor chain.
A request whose actor chain cannot be verified MUST be refused with `DELEGATION_REQUIRED`.
An `unattended` request MUST be accepted only under a delegation whose `modes` include `unattended`.
In `unattended` mode DSoR MUST take the subject from the delegation record, never from the request.
When more than one active delegation could cover an `unattended` request and the request names none, DSoR MUST refuse it with `DELEGATION_REQUIRED`.
Every decision record MUST state the identity mode and the source and time of the subject's authority.
A delegation MUST be revocable by its delegator and by a tenant administrator.
Revocation MUST take effect for new decisions within the bound of §44.
On revocation or expiry, every proposal created under the delegation that is `PENDING_APPROVAL` or `APPROVED` MUST move to `CANCELLED`.
Subdelegation MUST be denied unless the delegation allows it.
A subdelegation MUST grant no authority that its parent lacks.
A subdelegation MUST be refused when it would exceed the parent's declared maximum depth.
Consumption under a subdelegation MUST count against the root delegation's cumulative limits.
Cumulative limits MUST be enforced with atomic reserve, commit, and release operations in the control-plane store.
A reservation MUST be keyed by proposal id, so that re-evaluating the same proposal never reserves twice.
A reservation MUST stay held while its proposal is `PENDING_APPROVAL`, `APPROVED`, `EXECUTING`, or `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`.
A reservation MUST be released when its proposal reaches `FAILED`, `REJECTED`, `EXPIRED`, `CANCELLED`, `REVOKED`, or `INVALIDATED`.
A command that would exceed a limit MUST be refused with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.
Every tenant-owned resource MUST carry its `tenant_id`.
Tenant isolation MUST be enforced in at least two independent layers: DSoR core, and the connector or store.
Tenant isolation MUST NOT depend on agent behavior, prompts, or tool descriptions.
Caches, idempotency records, counters, holds, proposals, events, and audit partitions MUST be keyed by tenant.
An implementation MUST ship a cross-tenant test suite that exercises every operation with a foreign-tenant URI.
DSoR MUST support role-based access control using the `<resource>:<action>` permission format.
DSoR MUST deny any operation for which no permission is granted.
Authorization and control evaluation MUST support at least the outcomes `ALLOW`, `DENY`, and `REQUIRE_APPROVAL`.
When several controls apply, the most restrictive outcome MUST win: `DENY` over any `REQUIRE_*`, and any `REQUIRE_*` over `ALLOW`.
When several `REQUIRE_*` outcomes apply, all of them MUST be satisfied.
A principal of type `agent` MUST NOT act as an approver.
An approver MUST be of type `human`.
Outside owner-approval mode (§16.2), an approver MUST NOT appear in the requesting chain of the proposal: not the subject, not the delegator of any acting agent, not any actor.
Where a contract declares `sod.incompatible_with`, the same effective principal MUST NOT perform incompatible operations on the same resource instance; the attempt returns `SOD_VIOLATION`.
A delegation that grants an incompatible pair of permissions for the same resource type MUST be rejected at creation.
An approver MUST independently hold the contract's `approve_permission` and an approval limit that covers the amount under §9.
DSoR MUST resolve an approver role such as "CFO" to concrete principals at approval time and record the basis.
Where a control requires a quorum, the approvals MUST come from distinct principals.
Owner-approval mode MUST be enabled only by a human tenant owner.
Enabling or disabling owner-approval mode MUST be recorded in audit.
In owner-approval mode the approver MUST complete step-up authentication no more than five minutes before approving.
In owner-approval mode the approver MUST be shown the DSoR-rendered payload required by DSOR-APR-06a, at every conformance level.
In owner-approval mode DSoR MUST send a notification of every approval to a second channel registered by the owner.
In owner-approval mode DSoR MUST enforce a declared value ceiling above which approval by the delegator is refused.
In owner-approval mode a proposal that involves a new counterparty or changed payment details MUST NOT execute before a declared cooling-off period has passed since approval.
Every decision bundle produced under owner-approval mode MUST be marked `sod_mode: owner_approval`.
A conformance statement MUST disclose whether owner-approval mode is available.
A control MUST validate against `control.schema.json`, which requires a version, a condition, an effect, a status, a named human owner, and an authority reference.
A control with no governed source MUST declare `authority.system: local`.
Control conditions and contract predicates MUST be CEL expressions evaluated in the environment of Appendix B.
An expression MUST NOT have access to anything outside that environment: no network, no clock other than `now`, no caller-supplied state.
When a control condition fails to evaluate — missing field, type error, unconvertible amount — the control's effect MUST apply.
When a precondition predicate fails to evaluate, the predicate MUST be treated as false.
A control MUST be activated, modified, suspended, or retired only by its human control owner.
An agent principal MUST NOT activate a control.
Activation MUST run the control's test vectors and fail if any vector fails.
A control on a monetary threshold MUST include a test vector in a currency other than the threshold's and a test vector with an unconvertible currency.
A test vector that depends on a currency conversion MUST pin the rates it assumes.
DSoR MUST detect, within the bound of §44, that the authority a control cites has been superseded, and then mark the control `stale_authority` and notify its owner.
A stale control MUST NOT be dropped or skipped.
After its grace period, a stale control on a `HIGH` or `CRITICAL` operation MUST yield at least `REQUIRE_APPROVAL`.
Every decision record MUST identify each evaluated control by id and version, together with the authority reference and version in force.
DSoR MUST provide per-agent suspension and a tenant-wide agent freeze.
A suspension or freeze MUST take effect for new decisions within the bound of §44, without cooperation from the agent runtime.
While a suspension or freeze is active, a proposal from an affected agent MUST NOT enter `EXECUTING`.
A suspension or freeze MUST be lifted only by a human holding `control:suspend`.
Rate and velocity limits MUST be enforced server-side, per agent and per tenant.
DSoR MUST support operation freezes and connector circuit breakers.
Operational controls MUST be evaluated both when a proposal is created and when it is executed.
A field with no declared classification MUST be treated as `CONFIDENTIAL`.
For agent principals, DSoR MUST omit, mask, or tokenize any field above the agent's clearance or barred by the tenant's model-egress policy before the response leaves DSoR.
A response from which fields were withheld MUST list the redactions.
A token issued in place of a masked value MUST be usable as a command input only by the principal and tenant it was issued to.
Every query response MUST carry a classification label equal to the highest classification among the fields it contains.
Aggregations over `RESTRICTED` fields MUST enforce a declared minimum group size.
DSoR MUST enforce budgets on rows returned per agent principal and per delegation over a time window.
A row budget MUST NOT be keyed on an identifier the caller can mint, such as a caller-supplied task id.
Reads that return `CONFIDENTIAL` or `RESTRICTED` data MUST be audited with principal, actor chain, operation, resource scope, and row count.
A conformance statement MUST declare the regions in which the control-plane store, audit, and event channels are held.
Each connector MUST declare the region of the system it fronts.
The model-egress policy MUST be able to restrict egress by the region of the agent's model boundary.
Erasure of personal data held in a system of record MUST be performed by a DSoR command under the full pipeline.

Audit MUST refer to data subjects by pseudonymous identifier, with any personal values held in renderings encrypted under a per-subject key, so that destroying the key erases the values without breaking the audit chain.
Commands MUST pass through the pipeline steps in the order given.
An interface, connector, or operation MUST NOT skip a pipeline step that applies to it.
The decision — outcome, controls evaluated, and the reason for any `DENY` — MUST be durably recorded before the response is returned.
A durable intent record containing the proposal id, operation and version, payload hash, idempotency key, connector, and security context MUST be written before any side effect is attempted.
If the control-plane store cannot accept the decision or intent record, DSoR MUST NOT execute; the caller receives `EVIDENCE_STORE_UNAVAILABLE`.
Where the connector's store and the control-plane store share a transaction, the state change, the final outcome, and the outbox entry MUST commit atomically.
An intent record with no final outcome MUST be treated as `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`.
Every state-changing command in `execute` or `propose_only` mode MUST carry an idempotency key.
The key MUST be claimed by an atomic insert scoped to (tenant, calling principal, operation, key) that stores the payload hash.
A request whose key is already claimed with the same payload hash MUST return the recorded status or result without re-execution.
A request whose key is already claimed with a different payload hash MUST be refused with `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`.
Idempotency records MUST be retained for at least the minimum of §44.
Where the connector declares downstream idempotency, DSoR MUST pass a key derived from its own idempotency key to the underlying system.
A proposal MUST be executed at most once; the proposal id is the idempotency key of its execution.
Every command MUST declare its concurrency strategy.
An optimistic command MUST return `STALE_STATE` when the resource version differs from the version the decision was made on.
Every command MUST declare one of these execution semantics in its contract.
Every command result MUST state the execution semantics that applied.
A `COMPENSATABLE` or `SAGA` operation MUST name its compensating operations, which run under the full pipeline.
While a proposal is in flight, a second proposal for the same operation over the same `exclusive_over` resource MUST be refused with `CONFLICT`, naming the existing proposal.
A precondition over an available amount — an open balance, a credit limit, stock on hand — MUST count amounts committed to in-flight proposals as unavailable.
If DSoR cannot establish whether a side effect occurred, the proposal MUST enter `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`.
DSoR MUST NOT report an unknown outcome as success, as failure, or with an error code whose retry class allows a new attempt.
While a proposal is `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, a replay MUST return the current status without re-execution, unless the connector declares downstream idempotency.
A `NON_COMPENSATABLE` operation MUST be routed only to a connector that declares downstream idempotency or outcome lookup.
While a proposal is `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, DSoR MUST hold every resource named in the contract's `hold_on_unknown`; any other command that binds a held resource returns `RESOURCE_HELD`.
A reconciliation process MUST resolve every `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` proposal to `COMMITTED` or `FAILED` and record the evidence used.
Each `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` occurrence MUST raise an alert within the bound of §44.
An occurrence unresolved after the bound of §44 MUST escalate to a human.
An agent principal MUST NOT resolve an unknown outcome.
The permission checked for `proposal.approve` MUST be the `approve_permission` of the target operation's contract.
A `proposal.*` command MUST NOT itself yield `REQUIRE_APPROVAL`.
`proposal.approve` MUST be refused with `APPROVAL_MISMATCH` unless the `payload_hash` supplied by the approver equals the stored proposal's payload hash.
`proposal.execute` MUST execute the stored canonical payload of the proposal.
`proposal.execute` MUST NOT accept a payload from its caller.
An agent principal MUST NOT execute a proposal that was created under a delegation other than its own.
A proposal's payload MUST NOT be modified after creation; a change is a new proposal that names the one it supersedes, and the superseded proposal moves to `CANCELLED`.
Proposals MUST follow this state machine.
A proposal MUST NOT leave a terminal state.
Every proposal transition MUST be recorded with its actor and its cause.

An approval MUST validate against `approval.schema.json`, which binds it to the proposal, operation and version, tenant, resource URIs, payload hash, risk level, the control requirements it satisfies, the approvers and the basis of their authority, an expiry, and the bound state.
The payload hash MUST be computed over the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON of the stored input.
An approval MUST expire no later than the ceiling of §44.
An approval MUST be revocable by its approver until the proposal enters `EXECUTING`.
Executing a proposal MUST re-evaluate the target command's preconditions, controls, segregation of duties, limits, delegation, and operational controls against `CURRENT` state.
Each `REQUIRE_APPROVAL` outcome of the re-evaluation MUST be satisfied by unexpired, unrevoked approvals on this proposal that meet the role and quorum the current evaluation demands.

A proposal MUST move to `INVALIDATED` without executing when a precondition fails, a re-evaluated requirement is unsatisfied, a new `REQUIRE_*` or `DENY` outcome appears, or the stored payload hash does not verify.
When a bound control has a new active version at execution, DSoR MUST evaluate the new version and record both versions in the decision bundle.
A `CRITICAL` operation MUST use `strict_version` binding, under which any change to a bound resource version or a bound control version invalidates the approval.
`proposal.approve` MUST be accepted only in `direct` identity mode, from an approver authenticated to DSoR under their own credentials.
Input relayed through the requesting agent, its runtime, or its client MUST NOT count as approval evidence.
The approver MUST be shown a rendering of the stored payload and bound state that DSoR generates.
Agent-written summary or rationale shown to an approver MUST be labelled as unverified agent content.
Every query result MUST state `observed_at`, the `resource_version` where one exists, the connector, and the freshness mode actually delivered.
DSoR MUST NOT label a cached value `CURRENT`.
Preconditions of `HIGH` and `CRITICAL` commands MUST be evaluated on `CURRENT` reads unless the contract explicitly permits bounded staleness.
When the connector cannot deliver the required freshness, DSoR MUST return `FRESHNESS_UNSATISFIABLE` and not fall back to a cache.
Every error MUST validate against `error-envelope.schema.json`, carrying a code from this table or a documented extension code, a retry class, and correlation identifiers.
An error MUST NOT reveal the existence or attributes of a resource the caller is not authorized to read.
For a command, a connector error MUST NOT be mapped to a code with retry class `safe_same_key` unless the side effect provably did not occur.
Every command decision, every proposal transition, and every read covered by DSOR-CLS-05 MUST produce a durable audit record that validates against `audit-record.schema.json`.
Operational audit MUST NOT be stored only as agent memory.
Deleting context MUST NOT delete audit, authoritative state, or KSoR records.
For each consequential command DSoR MUST produce a decision bundle that validates against `decision-bundle.schema.json`.
Audit and compliance evidence MUST NOT depend on private model reasoning traces.
Information supplied by the agent about itself — skill, rationale, purpose, task id — MUST be recorded under `agent_asserted`.
Agent-asserted information MUST NOT be an input to authorization or control evaluation.
The DSoR runtime identity MUST NOT be able to update or delete audit records.
Audit records MUST be tamper-evident through hash chaining, signed checkpoints, or an equivalent mechanism.
Where audit is partitioned into several chains, every record MUST belong to exactly one chain.
Every audit chain MUST be covered by each checkpoint.
Audit records MUST hold payload hashes and classification-aware renderings, not raw copies of `RESTRICTED` values.
Reading audit MUST itself be authorized and audited.
Audit retention MUST be policy-controlled and support legal and compliance holds.
Where events are published, they MUST be produced through a transactional outbox or an equivalent that ties the event to the recorded outcome.
Every event MUST validate against `event.schema.json`, carrying a unique `event_id`, the resource URI, a per-resource ordering key, correlation identifiers, and `origin`.
An event MUST NOT contain `RESTRICTED` field values.
Event channels MUST be tenant-scoped.
DSoR MUST propagate `task_id`, `trace_id`, `session_id`, `tenant_id`, `agent_id`, `principal_id`, and `request_id` through connectors, audit, and events.
DSoR MUST generate a `request_id` when the caller supplies none.
Context MUST NOT be retrievable across tenants.
Where current state or current policy is material to a consequential command, the runtime MUST revalidate memory-derived facts against DSoR or KSoR before invoking the command.
Context derived from DSoR or KSoR data MUST carry its provenance and a classification at least as high as the highest-classified source field.
`RESTRICTED` values MUST NOT be persisted to the context store; the store keeps the resource URI and re-reads through DSoR.
An extracted memory MUST record whether untrusted external content was present in the task (`tainted: true`).
Memories MUST be presented to the model as data, never executed as instructions.
A tainted memory MUST NOT be promoted to a skill or to KSoR without human review.
Skills MUST be versioned and identified by content hash.
A skill MUST NOT contain usable connector credentials.
A skill used in a `HIGH` or `CRITICAL` operation MUST have been approved by a human owner at organization scope.
For operations rated `MEDIUM` and above, the runtime MUST report the skill URI, version, and hash with the command.
Agent context MUST NOT become organizational knowledge except through: agent observation → knowledge proposal → governance and human review → KSoR.

A memory provider MUST NOT store an operational attribute of a DSoR resource — its status, balance, amount, or approval state — as a remembered fact; it refers to the resource by canonical URI, and the agent reads the attribute through DSoR.
Every model that a context provider uses to extract, summarize, or embed content MUST be treated as a model boundary under the tenant's model-egress policy, exactly as the agent's own model is.
Every connector MUST publish a declaration that validates against `connector.schema.json`.
An operation MUST NOT be routed to a connector that lacks a capability the contract requires, unless the contract defines fallback semantics.
Connector credentials, refresh tokens, private keys, and database passwords MUST NOT be exposed to the model or the agent runtime.
Every connector MUST declare its `write_exclusivity`.
For a `shared` connector, `resource_version` MUST derive from the native version, ETag, or a content hash, not from a DSoR-side counter.
A `shared` connector MUST declare its change-detection method and maximum detection lag.
Events caused by writes that did not pass through DSoR MUST be marked `origin: external`.
A connector reachable by agents MUST be reachable only through the DSoR pipeline.
`dsor_runtime` MUST NOT be a superuser, hold `BYPASSRLS`, or own tenant tables.
Tenant tables MUST use `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`.
The tenant setting MUST be transaction-local.
A query executed with no tenant setting MUST yield no rows.
Remote deployments MUST publish Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728).
DSoR MUST reject an access token whose audience or resource (RFC 8707) is not this DSoR deployment.
Clients MUST validate the issuer per RFC 9207.
Public clients MUST use PKCE.
Dynamic Client Registration MUST be disabled by default; clients are identified with Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD).
In `on_behalf_of` mode the subject and actor chain MUST be conveyed with OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693): `sub` identifies the subject and nested `act` claims identify each actor.
In `unattended` mode the agent MUST authenticate with an asymmetric credential — `private_key_jwt` (RFC 7523) or mutual TLS (RFC 8705) — never a shared secret.
An `unattended` access token MUST identify the agent as `sub` and carry no subject claim for a human; DSoR takes the subject from the delegation record (DSOR-DEL-08).
An MCP tool name MUST be the operation id with `.` replaced by `_`: `invoice.get` → `invoice_get`, `proposal.execute` → `proposal_execute`.
`tools/list` MUST return only the operations inside the caller's effective authority.
The cache scope of a filtered catalog MUST prevent it from being shared across principals.
Every tool MUST set all four hints explicitly, derived from the operation contract by the table above.
A DSoR control MUST NOT depend on a client honoring a hint.
A `PENDING_APPROVAL` outcome MUST be returned as a structured, non-error tool result carrying the proposal URI.
The `proposal_get` tool MUST be available to every principal that can invoke a command.
MRTR input MUST NOT be accepted as approval evidence or as step-up authentication.
DSoR core MUST authorize on the parsed request body, not on the `Mcp-Method` or `Mcp-Name` headers.
A request whose routing headers and body disagree MUST be rejected.
DSoR MUST version the protocol, entity schemas, operations, connector contracts, and controls.
A breaking change MUST produce a new major version (`payment.execute@1` → `payment.execute@2`).
Audit records and decision bundles MUST record the versions that applied.
A deprecated operation or schema version MUST keep working until its published deprecation window closes.
A proposal created for `operation@N` MUST NOT be executed as any other version.
A conformance statement MUST declare a value for every parameter in this table, within the limit for the claimed level.
A tenant-level setting MUST NOT loosen a parameter beyond the limit for the claimed level.
A conformance statement MUST give the level claimed, the specification version, and — for RP — the bindings implemented.
